items.followUp: State the rules for writing the scientific name of an organism.

rubric.why: A binomial name consists of two parts: the genus name and the species name.
rubric.description: States that a scientific name has two words, the genus and species names.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two parts of the name.

rubric.why: The genus begins with a capital letter and the species name begins with a lowercase letter.
rubric.description: Gives the capitalization rule for the two names.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both capitalization conventions.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature gives each organism a two-word scientific name: the genus name followed by the species name.
The genus name begins with a capital letter, while the species name begins with a lowercase letter; the names are written in italics or underlined separately when handwritten.

items.followUp: What is the function of sclerenchyma tissue?

rubric.why: Collenchyma cells are living and characteristically have walls thickened unevenly at the corners.
rubric.description: Describes the living cells and their unevenly thickened walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the living nature and corner thickening.

rubric.why: Collenchyma supports growing plant parts while allowing them to bend without breaking.
rubric.description: States its role in support and flexibility of young plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for support and flexibility in young parts.

modelAnswer: Collenchyma is a simple permanent tissue made of living, elongated cells with walls unevenly thickened at the corners.
It provides support and flexibility to young parts of the plant, such as stems and leaves.

items.followUp: What are enzymes, and how do they affect chemical reactions in living organisms?

rubric.why: Biocatalysts are catalysts that operate in living organisms.
Catalysts increase reaction rate without being used up in the reaction.
rubric.description: States their effect on reactions and that they are not consumed.

modelAnswer: Biocatalysts are biological catalysts, usually enzymes, that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms.
They are not used up or permanently changed in the reactions they catalyse.

items.followUp: How does a substrate bind to an enzyme?

rubric.why: The active site is the particular region of an enzyme to which its substrate binds.
rubric.description: Defines the active site as the enzyme region where the substrate binds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating substrate binding on a specific enzyme region.

rubric.why: The enzyme-catalysed reaction takes place at the active site.
rubric.description: States that catalysis occurs at the active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the role of the active site in the reaction.

modelAnswer: The active site is the specific region of an enzyme to which its substrate binds.
The enzyme-catalysed reaction takes place at this site.

items.followUp: Why is ATP called the energy currency of the cell?

rubric.why: Energy is stored in the chemical bonds between ATP’s phosphate groups.
rubric.description: States that ATP stores energy in its phosphate bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying energy storage in ATP.

rubric.why: ATP releases energy that cells use to carry out their activities.
rubric.description: States that ATP supplies energy for cellular activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining how cells use ATP.

modelAnswer: ATP stores energy in the bonds between its phosphate groups.
When energy is needed, ATP releases it for cellular activities; therefore, ATP acts as the cell’s energy currency.

rubric.why: Lactic acid fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose to form lactic acid.
rubric.description: Identifies the anaerobic conversion of glucose into lactic acid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the absence of oxygen and the product, lactic acid.

rubric.why: This process releases only a small amount of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that little energy is released.

modelAnswer: Lactic acid fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose to form lactic acid.
It releases only a small amount of energy.

items.followUp: State one role of magnesium in plant life.

rubric.why: Potassium activates several enzymes in plants.
Potassium helps regulate the opening and closing of stomata.
rubric.description: States potassium’s role in regulating stomata.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its role in stomatal regulation.

modelAnswer: Potassium activates several enzymes in plants.
It also helps regulate the opening and closing of stomata.

items.followUp: What is compost, and how does it improve soil?

rubric.why: Organic fertilizers are natural materials made from plant or animal matter.
rubric.description: Defines organic fertilizer by its natural plant or animal origin.

rubric.why: Farmyard manure and compost are examples of organic fertilizers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: An organic fertilizer is a natural material made from plant or animal matter and added to soil to improve its fertility.
